# S01: Supabase Schema & Project Setup

**Established OACP foundation: Supabase schema, Edge Function router, shared types, SDK scaffold, and monorepo structure**

## What Happened

Set up the complete OACP project foundation: initialized Supabase with a Postgres migration for the agents table (Ed25519 identity, GIN-indexed capabilities, RLS, Realtime), created the Edge Function skeleton with a fat-function router pattern (health check live, other routes stubbed), defined shared TypeScript types for the full protocol (Agent Card, Message Envelope, API contracts), scaffolded the oacp-sdk npm package, and established the monorepo structure with npm workspaces. All committed with a comprehensive README.

## Verification

Structural validation of all files (SQL migration 10/10 checks, Edge Function 7/7 symbols, types 5/5 types). Git commit of 26 files succeeded.

## Requirements Advanced

- REQ-REG-01 — Agents table schema supports registration and Agent Card storage
- REQ-REG-03 — agent_id UUID PK, created_at/updated_at timestamps defined
- REQ-DISC-01 — GIN index on capabilities and status filter support defined

## Requirements Validated

None.

## New Requirements Surfaced

None.

## Requirements Invalidated or Re-scoped

None.

## Deviations

Docker/Deno not available locally, so migrations and Edge Functions couldn't be tested against live environments. Validated structurally instead.

## Known Limitations

Cannot test against live Supabase locally without Docker. Edge Functions not type-checked without Deno.

## Follow-ups

Install Deno locally for Edge Function type checking. Set up Docker for local Supabase stack testing.

## Files Created/Modified

- `package.json` — Monorepo root with npm workspaces
- `supabase/config.toml` — Supabase project config (project_id: oacp)
- `supabase/migrations/20250331000001_create_agents_table.sql` — Agents table with Ed25519 identity, GIN-indexed capabilities, RLS, Realtime
- `supabase/functions/oacp/index.ts` — OACP Edge Function with router, health check, stub routes
- `supabase/functions/_shared/types.ts` — Shared TypeScript types for Agent Card, Message Envelope, API contracts

decisions.decision: Deployment platform for OACP backend API
decisions.choice: Supabase Edge Functions (Deno) for API + Postgres + Realtime; Vercel for web dashboard only; Render for reference agent runtime
decisions.rationale: Supabase provides the full stack needed: Edge Functions for REST API, Postgres for persistence, Realtime for WebSocket pub-sub message bus. Vercel is serverless-only (not suited for persistent agent processes). Render provides persistent Node.js for always-on agent heartbeating. This maps to user's stated deployment preferences.

decisions.decision: iOS app vs web dashboard for demo observer UI
decisions.choice: Build web-based observer dashboard first; defer iOS SwiftUI app to a later milestone
decisions.rationale: iOS app is a significant scope addition (SwiftUI, Supabase Swift SDK, separate build toolchain). A web dashboard achieves the same observer/controller goal with same TypeScript stack, 1/5th the effort. iOS can follow as a separate milestone once the protocol is proven.
decisions.revisable: Yes — can add iOS milestone later

decisions.choice: @noble/ed25519 v3.x for Ed25519 keypair generation, message signing, and verification
decisions.rationale: 5KB, zero dependencies, RFC8032/FIPS-186-5 compliant, SUF-CMA secure, works in Node.js/Deno/browsers. Most widely-used pure-JS Ed25519 implementation (788 dependents). Async and sync APIs available.

decisions.choice: Align OACP Agent Card with A2A Agent Card structure where possible; add protocols_supported field for future A2A bridging
decisions.rationale: A2A is now the dominant agent-to-agent standard (150+ orgs, Linux Foundation governance). Aligning schema structure makes future interop easier. OACP adds registry/relay primitives that A2A lacks, so compatibility is complementary not redundant.
